docs.title: Other telegrams on supervised lines
docs.text:
Three more telegrams accompany the supervision round (the fourth captured one, 0x33/0x01, is the Roll Call). Genius Gateway names 0x22/0x00 Line Clock in the packet visualizer; the family 0x11 is still shown as Unknown. It takes them as a sign of life of the sending module.

Family / Type Length Flags Repetitions Seen Function 0x11 / 0x00 30 B 0x48 about 350 Long burst after a commissioning and on a module failure; the two payload bytes were always B6 08. Forwarded. Opens a supervision round. B6 08 is a constant; its meaning is open. 0x11 / 0x01 28 B 0x28 11 Twice, 2 s before the radio link fault. Sent after the last Module Missing of a round's report phase. 0x22 / 0x00 33 B 0x08 23 About 90 s after every 0x11/0x00. Payload: hour, minute and second of the line's own clock and a 16-bit day counter. Forwarded. Sent 89 s after 0x11/0x00: distributes the line's own clock (3 clock bytes + 16-bit day counter after 22 00). Receivers presumably set their clock by it.

The family 0x11 is not specific to the FM Pro X: FM Basis X modules can send both of its telegrams as well (0x11/0x00 with a 16-bit value, 0x11/0x01 without payload). What family 0x11 means beyond the supervision round is open.

docs.title: Line Addressing: Line Code and Line-ID
docs.text:
A radio module belongs to its line by two values, and a packet has to match both of them:

Line code Line-ID Size 1 byte 32 bit Comes from the two rotary switches of the module (FM Pro X, old FM Basis / FM Pro); fixed to A.0 on an FM Basis X the radio commissioning - generated there, effectively random, stored by every module of the line In a packet offset 3 (addressed line), 8 (originator), 13 (forwarder) offset 18–21 Purpose separates the lines within one installation and is the basis of the collective alarm separates installations: neighbouring systems use the same rotary positions, but not the same ID

This is what the manufacturer describes: after commissioning, a module only reacts to packets carrying both the same line and the same identification code; neighbouring systems are ignored.3

Corrected in v1.6.0

Up to v1.5.0 this page called the rotary position ("group/line") display metadata that the modules never compare, listed the bytes 3, 8 and 13 as an address mode and two unknown constants, and assumed that old FM Basis / FM Pro modules have no commissioned ID. All of that was wrong: the rotary position is transmitted in every packet and is part of the receive and forward filter, and old modules are commissioned by radio as well.

docs.title: Line code
docs.text:
line code = letter << 4 | number: the high nibble is the first rotary switch (0 = A … 7 = H), the low nibble the second one (0–9).

Rotary position Line code A.0 0x00 A.3 0x03 C.3 0x23 H.7 0x77 every line (Dst-Line only) 0xFF

Seen in captures: 0x00 in all packets of FM Basis X modules, 0x03 at the offsets 3, 8 and 13 in the packets of two FM Pro X modules (see the examples under Radio Link Supervision). The same byte appears in the acoustic readout (byte 29) and in the ConfigCheckProbe response (offset 30).

docs.title: Receiving
docs.text:
A module accepts a packet when all three conditions hold:

  1. Dst-SN (offset 4–7) is its own serial number or FF FF FF FF,
  2. Dst-Line (offset 3) is its own line code or 0xFF,
  3. Line-ID (offset 18–21) is its own Line-ID or FF FF FF FF - or the module has no Line-ID yet (0).

A packet that fails one of them is only accepted as a collective alarm.

Observed on a line of eleven FM Basis X modules (line code 0x00): a line test start addressed to its Line-ID made all detectors signal and was forwarded by the modules. The same packet with the line code 0x01 (A.1) at the offsets 3, 8 and 13 - flags and everything else unchanged - left every detector silent, and no module forwarded it. The following stop with the line code 0x00 was forwarded by all of them.

docs.title: Forwarding
docs.text: A module forwards a packet of its own line: Org-Line (offset 8) equals its own line code and condition 3 above holds. On forwarding it writes its own line code and serial number into Fwd-Line and Fwd-SN. Forward class and hop limit apply as described under Forwarding; a packet of another line is only forwarded as a collective alarm.

docs.title: Collective alarm lines
docs.text:
The letter H stands for the collective alarm lines (Sammelalarm; FM Pro and FM Pro X only). A module with DIP switch 4 (Receive Collective Alarm) switched on also accepts and forwards packets of other lines, if the packet carries the collective bit (bit 4 of Flags, offset 24) and the two line codes are paired:

Collective line Paired with H.0 A, B H.1 C, D H.2 E, F H.4 A, B, C H.5 D, E, F H.7 A – G and H.0, H.1, H.2, H.4, H.5
  • The pairing works in both directions: a module on a line A.x accepts collective packets from H.0, H.4 and H.7.
  • For the lines A – G only the letter counts here, not the number.
  • H.3, H.6, H.8 and H.9 are paired with nothing.
  • The Line-ID is not compared for a collective packet.

Collective packets were not captured so far; nothing of this was verified on air.

docs.title: FM Basis X
docs.text:
• No rotary switches: the line code is permanently 0x00 (A.0). No DIP switches either, so no collective alarm.
  • It follows that FM Basis X modules only work together with modules whose rotary switches are set to A.0 - the manufacturer's rule for mixed operation with old modules.3
  • Over smartsonic acoustic readout, bytes 25–28 carry the commissioned 32-bit lineId (non-zero once commissioned; 0 = unassigned) and byte 29 the line code.

docs.title: Old generation - FM Basis and FM Pro
docs.text:
• Two rotary switches (letter A–G/H, number 0–9; the manufacturer speaks of up to 70 lines). Factory default is A.0.
  • The modules are commissioned by radio as well, and the commissioning gives them a 32-bit Line-ID. Reported for an installation with FM Pro modules and a used FM Basis from 2014 (#33):
    • A module that is inserted with its rotary switches set like those of the others (A.1) does not join their line. Its Line-ID is 0 ("not set"), and it starts a commissioning of its own.
    • A commissioning started on a detector that already belongs to the line takes new modules into that line: they adopt its Line-ID. A commissioning started on a new detector opens a new line with a new Line-ID - with the rotary switches unchanged.
    • So the rotary position alone does not make a line. As on the X generation, both values count.
  • Over smartsonic, an old module transmits only its type and serial number - not the radio dataset. The acoustic lineId (bytes 25–28) reads 0. The Line-ID of an old module is therefore only visible on air, in the packets it sends.
  • Open: whether old modules carry their line code at the offsets 3, 8 and 13 like the X generation was not checked against a capture yet.

docs.title: Observed Line-IDs
docs.text: Radio module Rotary position Line-ID (hex) Line-ID (dec) old FM Basis A.0 0xD7F75240 3623309888 FM Pro (see #33) A.1 0x5608E5E6 1443423718 FM Basis X A.0 (fixed) 0xA9B22DF3 2847026675

docs.title: What the gateway makes of it
docs.text:
• Receiving. The gateway listens to every packet, whatever its line code and Line-ID. It keys alarm lines on the Line-ID. The line code of the originator (Org-Line) gives the line setting of a detector with an FM Pro X or a module of unknown type, and of an alarm line that is added from the packet or whose detectors do not tell it - never from a packet originated by a gateway. The packet visualizer shows all three line codes.
  • Alarm line of a detector. It is taken over from the radio packets of its module: an alarm, a status change, a line test or a telegram of the radio link supervision names the Line-ID. For old modules that is the only source, see Device Management. Their rotary position is entered by hand.
  • Transmitting. Line test, fire alarm and commissioning packets of the gateway carry the line setting of the alarm line at the offsets 3, 8 and 13. Up to v1.6.0 it was always 0x00 (A.0), and by the receive rule above modules set to another rotary position did not accept them - observed with the line code the other way round: a line test start with the line code 0x01 was ignored by a line set to A.0 (see Receiving). It fits the report in #33 that a commissioning started by the gateway had no effect on a line set to A.1. The range test is not affected: its ConfigCheckProbe addresses every line.
  • Old modules were observed not to answer the ConfigCheckProbe of the range test.

  1. See Packet Fragmentation section for details on the 64-byte total packet size limit that constrains the maximum payload to 59 bytes in practice. ↩↩

  2. Genius Gateway uses FF FF FF FE (4294967294) as serial number when it sends packets. See Alarm Lines Management for more information. ↩↩

  3. Source: Hekatron Bedienungsanleitung Funkmodul Basis X / Pro X (7003145), section "Identifikationscode", and Genius Funksysteme im Mischbetrieb whitepaper (7050644). ↩↩

docs.title: Protocol Captures
docs.text: Logic analyzer traces for CC1101 communication, as well as UART and EEPROM communication, can be found here.

docs.title: Peripheral Interfaces
docs.text:
The radio module's microcontroller communicates with three peripheral devices using two serial interfaces.

The MSP430 communicates with the CC1101 RF transceiver and the EEPROM via a shared SPI bus .

The MSP430 communicates via the 6-pin header with the smoke detector's microcontroller over a 2-wire UART .

docs.title: Measurement Device
docs.text: For recording the serial communication, I used the DSLogic U3Pro16 logic analyzer, which was very well suited for this task.

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
The logic analyzers from DreamSourceLab use the freely available open-source software DSView ( GitHub Repository ) for visualizing and exporting traces. DSView can also be used without a logic analyzer to load and analyze traces.

DSView is a clone of the open-source tool PulseView (sigrok) ( GitHub Repository ).

docs.title: Decoders
docs.text:
The performance of an analysis tool like DSView or PulseView is largely determined by the number and analysis scope of supported buses and protocols. Multi-layer protocol decoder stacks significantly facilitate evaluation.

The following decoders should be installed for evaluating the trace files:

docs.title: Trace files
docs.text: File Content CC1101 EEPROM UART  startup_new-rm.dsl Radio module is plugged onto the smoke detector.  mounting-to-base.dsl Interface communication when the smoke detector (with attached radio module) is twisted into the base.  comissioning-master.dsl Interface communication of the radio module that initiates commissioning.  comissioning-slave.dsl Interface communication of the radio module that participates in commissioning.  linetest-start-stop.dsl Alarm line test is started and stopped.  firealarm-start-stop.dsl Fire alarm is triggered and ended on a smoke detector.

docs.title: Captures by contributors
docs.text: Source Content danielrdt/genius-log: Radio link supervision, raw captures  Packets of a line with two FM Pro X modules and radio link supervision switched on, recorded with the gateway's WebSocket logger over 14 days: daily supervision series, module missing, radio link fault and its muting, commissioning. Basis of Radio Link Supervision. danielrdt/genius-log: Genius telegrams  Overview of all telegrams seen on that line with counts, forwarding and timing, including the line clock and the drift of the daily series.

docs.title: UART Analysis
docs.text: The radio module and the smoke detector's microcontroller exchange data over a 2-wire UART on the 6-pin header. The smoke detector is the host: it polls the radio module with short command frames, and the radio module answers each command with a response frame. Recorded UART communication is available in the Trace files.

docs.title: Frame format
docs.text:
Every frame - in both directions - has the same structure:

+--------+--------+------------------------+--------+
|  TYPE  |  LEN   |   payload (LEN-1 B)     |  XOR   |
+--------+--------+------------------------+--------+
Field Size Description TYPE 1 Frame type / purpose. Commands from the detector use low values (0x01–0x13); responses from the radio module use 0xAx. LEN 1 Number of bytes that follow, including the checksum - so the whole frame is LEN + 2 bytes long. payload LEN-1 Command arguments or response data. XOR 1 Error-detection byte: an XOR over the preceding bytes of the frame.

Frames are delimited by timing: a gap of more than roughly 0.8 s between bytes resets the receiver to the start of a new frame.

docs.title: Commands and responses
docs.text:
The detector issues read/query commands; each is answered by a matching 0xAx response. None of the observed commands writes data or triggers a radio transmission.

Cmd Resp Purpose 0x01 0xA1 Report the radio module's firmware version 0x02 0xA2 Report a status flag 0x0A 0xA6 Read the configuration block 0x0E 0xA7 Report the number of stored node records 0x0F 0xA8 Read stored node record N (record index in the payload) 0x10 0xA9 Read the module identity / serial number 0x13 0xAA Read a block of the EEPROM

In addition, the radio module reports link quality to the detector with a 0xA4 response after a range / connection test.

docs.title: Payloads
docs.text:
• Version (0xA1) - the firmware version of the radio module.
  • Status (0xA2) - a status flag byte.
  • Record count (0xA7) - the number of commissioned peer modules stored in the module's node database.
  • Record read (0xA8) - a single node record (a peer serial number and its associated data) from the database, selected by the index sent with 0x0F.
  • Identity (0xA9) - the module's own serial number.
  • Config / EEPROM block (0xA6 / 0xAA) - raw bytes from the module's EEPROM configuration and storage regions.

Known structures visible in the payloads include serial numbers, the current time (hour / minute / second), version bytes, and error-detection (XOR) at the end of each transmission.

docs.title: Setting up Genius Gateway
docs.text: This guide walks you through the complete setup process for Genius Gateway, from initial hardware assembly and software installation to network configuration and integration with your smart home system.

docs.title: General Setup
docs.text:
The foundation of your Genius Gateway deployment. This page covers:

  • Hardware Assembly: Experimental breadboard setup or final PCB assembly
  • Development Environment: Installing VSCode with Pioarduino IDE
  • Software Build: Cloning repository, configuring target board, building firmware
  • Initial Flash: Uploading firmware and accessing the web interface for the first time
  • Basic connectivity: Connecting to WiFi network and to MQTT broker, setting up user authorization

docs.title: Configure Gateway
docs.text:
Smoke detector and alarm line configuration for full functionality:

  • Integration Levels: Basic alarm detection (no configuration), advanced device integration (Home Assistant), alarm line functions (line tests, fire alarm tests)
  • Adding Smoke Detectors: Import from backup, manual entry with serial numbers, automatic discovery
  • Alarm Line Configuration: Import from backup, manual registration, automatic discovery via line test

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
External service integration for smart home and time synchronization:

  • MQTT Configuration: Connect to MQTT broker (encrypted/unencrypted), configure authentication and connection parameters, set up simple alarm and fault publishing and Home Assistant MQTT Discovery
  • NTP Setup: Configure time server, select timezone with automatic DST handling, ensure accurate timestamps for logging

docs.title: WiFi
docs.text:
Network connectivity configuration for both normal operation and fallback scenarios:

  • WiFi Station Mode: Connect as a client to your existing WiFi network, configure hostname (mDNS), manage multiple networks with priority or signal strength selection
  • Access Point Mode: Provide fallback WiFi network for initial setup or when station connection fails, configure SSID, password, channel, and IP addressing

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
Security and access control configuration:

  • User Accounts: Create, edit, and delete users with different privilege levels (admin/guest)
  • JWT Security: Configure JWT secret for authentication token generation
  • Authentication Flow: Understand login process, session management, and token-based authentication

docs.title: System
docs.text:
Ongoing monitoring, maintenance, and firmware management:

  • System Status: Real-time monitoring of hardware, memory, network, and radio module status
  • Diagnostics: System metrics, check radio module connectivity, download core dump
  • Firmware Updates: OTA updates, upload new firmware
  • Device Actions: Restart, factory reset

docs.title: Basic Function
docs.text:
The simplest setup that can detect fire alarms from nearby radio-networked Genius Plus X smoke detectors and forward them to a smart home system without explicit configuration of smoke detectors and alarm lines in Genius Gateway is:

  • Basic configuration (WiFi, MQTT broker) has been performed
  • Processing of alarms from unknown smoke detectors is enabled in the Gateway Settings
  • Simple Alarm Publishing via a central topic is configured (optionally including battery warnings and faults)

docs.title: Advanced Integration (Home Assistant Compatible)
docs.text:
If existing radio-networked Genius Plus X smoke detectors are to be integrated as devices in Home Assistant, they must be added in Genius Gateway.

More details about the possibilities in interaction with Home Assistant are described in Smart Home Integration.

Changes to the configuration in Genius Gateway (e.g., adjusting the location) are also synchronized to Home Assistant.

docs.title: Alarm Line Functions
docs.text:
Additional functions are available when alarm lines are configured in Genius Gateway:

  • Line tests
  • Fire alarm tests

docs.title: Importing Smoke Detectors
docs.text: If smoke detectors were previously configured and exported with Genius Gateway, they can be imported again.

docs.title: Manually Adding Smoke Detectors
docs.text:
To add smoke detectors, proceed as follows:

  1. Twist the smoke detector out of the socket.
  2. Determine the serial number and production date of the radio module and the smoke detector and write them down
  3. Add the smoke detector in the Genius Gateway web interface

Repeat these steps for each smoke detector that should be integrated into Home Assistant.

docs.title: Determining Serial Numbers and Production Dates
docs.text:
The Genius Plus X smoke detectors come in two variants, which can be distinguished by the color of the batteries:

  • Purple batteries: older version
  • Blue batteries: newer version

docs.title: Older Smoke Detector Version
docs.text:
On the older smoke detector version, the serial number of the smoke detector is unfortunately covered by the radio module. To read the serial number, the radio module must be temporarily removed.

Meaning of the markings:

  • Serial number and production date of the smoke detector
  • Serial number and production date of the radio module

  • Older detector with mounted radio module The radio module covers the smoke detector's serial number.

  • Older detector without radio module As soon as the radio module is removed, the smoke detector's serial number is revealed.

New Commissioning Required

When the radio module is removed from the smoke detector, the radio module loses its association with an alarm line. After reading the serial number of the smoke detector and correctly placing the radio module back on the smoke detector, commissioning for alarm line formation must be performed again according to the manufacturer's instructions.

docs.title: Newer Smoke Detector Version
docs.text:
On the newer smoke detector version, the serial number of the smoke detector can be read without removing the radio module.

Meaning of the markings:

  • Serial number and production date of the smoke detector
  • Serial number and production date of the radio module

  • Newer detector with mounted radio module The serial number is perfectly readable on the newer detector version.

  • Newer detector with revealed production date To read the production date more easily, the radio module can be slightly lifted without interrupting the connection between radio module and smoke detector.

Radio Module Must Remain Securely Connected

If the radio module has been lifted too much so that the connection to the smoke detector was interrupted, the radio module has also lost its association with an alarm line. This can be recognized by the fact that the test button of the radio module lights up green-yellow-red after screwing it back into the socket.

In this case, commissioning for alarm line formation must be performed again according to the manufacturer's instructions.

docs.title: Adding Alarm Lines
docs.text:
There are three ways to configure alarm lines:

  1. Import from a backup (not recommended)
  2. Manual addition (not recommended)
  3. Alarm line discovery (recommended)

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
Import Alarm Lines Only in Exceptional Cases

Alarm lines should only be imported for testing and development purposes, as after import it cannot be guaranteed that the actual alarm lines still correspond to those previously configured.

Importing alarm lines is done through the web interface.

docs.title: Manually Adding Alarm Lines
docs.text:
Manually Add Alarm Lines Only in Exceptional Cases

Alarm lines should only be manually added for testing and development purposes, as after creation it cannot be guaranteed that the actual alarm lines correspond to those manually specified.

Manually adding alarm lines is done through the web interface.

docs.title: Alarm Line Discovery
docs.text:
This is the safest method to determine and save the currently existing alarm line (or alarm lines).

  1. Log in to the Genius Gateway web interface.
  2. Make sure that automatic addition of alarm lines from all received packet types is enabled in the Gateway Settings.
  3. Switch to Alarm Line Management in the web interface.

  4. Initiate a line test on one of the installed smoke detectors for an existing alarm line according to the manufacturer's operating instructions:

    • Twist a smoke detector of an alarm line out of the socket
    • Shortly press (< 5 seconds) the red control button on the radio module

    All reachable and functional smoke detectors will now begin to signal the test. Let the line test run until the new alarm line is visible in the web interface. 5. Abort the line test: - Shortly press the red control button again - Twist the smoke detector back into the socket 6. Edit the alarm line and give it a meaningful name.

Repeat the procedure if multiple alarm lines should be configured.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: The Connections pages configure external network services that the Genius Gateway can integrate with, including MQTT for smart home integration and NTP for accurate time synchronization.

docs.title: MQTT
docs.text: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) is a lightweight messaging protocol ideal for IoT devices and smart home integration. The Genius Gateway can publish device states and alarm events to an MQTT broker for integration with home automation systems like Home Assistant.

docs.title: MQTT Status
docs.text: The MQTT status section displays self-explaning real-time connection information.

docs.title: General Settings
docs.text:
Click the General Settings collapsible section to configure MQTT connection parameters.

Administrator Access Required

MQTT settings can only be modified by users with administrator privileges.

docs.title: Connection Settings
docs.text:
Enable MQTT

Toggle to enable or disable MQTT functionality. When disabled, no MQTT connections or publishing occur.

URI

The MQTT broker URI is composed of three separate fields: a Protocol dropdown, a Host input (hostname or IPv4 address), and a Port input. The fields are validated independently and assembled into a <protocol>://<host>:<port> URI behind the scenes.

Supported protocols and their default ports:

  • mqtt:// - unencrypted MQTT over TCP, default port 1883
  • mqtts:// - MQTT over TLS/SSL, default port 8883
  • ws:// - MQTT over unencrypted WebSocket, default port 80
  • wss:// - MQTT over WebSocket Secure (TLS), default port 443

Automatic Port Updates

Switching the protocol updates the port field to the new protocol's default - but only if the current port still matches the previous protocol's default. Custom ports you have set are preserved across protocol changes.

Username

Optional username for MQTT broker authentication. Leave empty if the broker doesn't require authentication.

Password

Optional password for MQTT broker authentication. Leave empty if the broker doesn't require authentication.

Password Storage

Passwords are stored unencrypted in the device's file system. Ensure physical access to the device is restricted.

Client ID

Unique identifier for this MQTT client. Each device connecting to the same broker must have a unique client ID.

Keep Alive

MQTT keep-alive interval in seconds (1-600). The device sends a ping to the broker if no other messages are sent within this interval to maintain the connection.

Publish Message Interval

Minimum interval between published MQTT messages in milliseconds (0-1000).

Disable Rate Limiting

0 = no rate limiting. Messages will be sent immediately.

This rate limiting may be used to prevent overwhelming the broker with rapid updates, if necessary.

Clean Session

When enabled, the broker discards all information about previous sessions when the client connects.

  • Enabled (checked): Start with a clean slate, no retained messages or subscriptions
  • Disabled (unchecked): Resume previous session with retained messages and subscriptions

Session Persistence

Genius Gateway does not rely on the MQTT broker's persistence function, as it publishes the state of all smoke detectors to the broker on every reconnect.

It is therefore recommended to enable this feature to ensure a consistent state and stable connection at all times.

Applying Changes

Click Apply Settings to save and apply the MQTT configuration. The device will reconnect to the MQTT broker with the new settings.

docs.title: Home Assistant Integration
docs.text:
The Home Assistant Integration collapsible card enables MQTT Discovery and configures the gateway's device identity in Home Assistant.

Administrator Access Required

Home Assistant settings can only be modified by users with administrator privileges.

Enable Home Assistant Integration

Toggle to enable/disable publishing with MQTT Discovery support for:

  • Gateway device with diagnostic sensors and remote controls
  • Individual detector configurations and states
  • Alarm line controls (if configured)

Disabling removes the device from Home Assistant

When this toggle is turned off while MQTT is connected, the gateway immediately sends empty retained payloads to all discovery topics, causing Home Assistant to remove the gateway device and all its entities. Re-enabling will re-register everything on the next save.

Discovery Prefix

Home Assistant MQTT Discovery prefix. All device discovery messages will use this prefix followed by the component type (e.g., binary_sensor, button, sensor). Default: homeassistant/.

Example: Using the default prefix creates discovery topics like:

  • homeassistant/binary_sensor/genius-gateway-<id>/…/config (smoke detector)
  • homeassistant/button/genius-gateway-<id>/…/config (alarm line button)

Home Assistant compatibility

The prefix must match the discovery_prefix configured in your Home Assistant instance.

Device Name

Name shown in Home Assistant's device registry. The factory default is Genius Gateway (<device MAC>) (e.g. Genius Gateway (1a2b3c4d5e6f)), so multiple units on the same network are distinguishable without any manual configuration.

Renaming is safe

The Device Name is purely cosmetic - it only sets the label Home Assistant displays. MQTT topics and the gateway's identity in HA's device registry are derived from the firmware name and the device's MAC address, so renaming never moves topics, never orphans entities, and never creates a second device in Home Assistant.

This was not the case up to v1.5.0, where renaming re-identified the gateway and left the previous device behind as a ghost. See the upgrade note below.

MQTT topics changed in v1.6.0

Firmware v1.6.0 restructured the Home Assistant topic tree. Base topics lost a redundant namespace level and no longer embed the MAC address twice:

v1.5.0  homeassistant/genius-gateway-1a2b3c4d5e6f/genius-gateway-1a2b3c4d5e6f-1a2b3c4d5e6f/…
v1.6.0  homeassistant/genius-gateway-1a2b3c4d5e6f/…

The upgrade cleans up after itself. On the first MQTT connect after flashing v1.6.0, the gateway clears every retained discovery config and state message it previously published under the old tree - always retiring an old config immediately before publishing its replacement - so Home Assistant drops the stale entity before registering the new one.

What this means for your setup:

  • Smoke detectors and alarm lines are untouched. Their discovery topics never contained the Device Name, and their unique_id is unchanged, so Home Assistant updates them in place. Entity IDs, history, and automations all survive.
  • The gateway's own entities (status, free heap, core temperature, restart button, the configuration switches, the firmware update entity) are re-registered under the new device identity. Because the old configs are cleared first, they reclaim their previous entity IDs, so automations referencing them keep working and recorder history - which is keyed by entity ID - is retained.

Two things are worth checking afterwards:

  • Home Assistant Settings Devices & Services MQTT: if a duplicate gateway device is still listed after a restart of Home Assistant, delete it manually.
  • Your MQTT broker: retained messages the gateway had published before, but no longer publishes at all (for example entities removed in an earlier firmware version), are not covered by the automatic cleanup. Browsing the broker with a tool like MQTT Explorer and deleting anything left under the old path removes the last remnants.

The automatic cleanup runs on every boot as long as an old-style tree could exist, so a gateway that was offline during the upgrade still cleans up whenever it next connects.

Manufacturer / Model

Optional labels shown in the Home Assistant device info panel. Useful for multi-gateway deployments to distinguish individual units.

Build-time Model Customization

If -D HW_VERSION=\"...\" is set in the build flags, it is automatically appended to the model default (e.g. Genius Gateway v1.0).

Update entity IDs when a detector's location changes

Opt-in, off by default. Home Assistant builds an entity ID once, when an entity is first registered, and never changes it afterwards. Renaming a detector's location in the gateway therefore leaves IDs such as sensor.hallway_genius_plus_x_alarm_line untouched.

With this option enabled:

  • Detectors are named after their location in Home Assistant instead of their model. The model name is used when no location is set.
  • Every detector gets explicit entity IDs of the form <domain>.<location>_<entity>, for example binary_sensor.living_room_smoke_detector or sensor.living_room_alarm_line. The location is reduced the way Home Assistant does it itself: lower case, letters with diacritics become their base letter (Küche kuche, ß ss), everything else becomes an underscore.
  • Changing a location renames the entities of that detector. The gateway removes them from Home Assistant, waits a few seconds and publishes them again with the new IDs. A progress dialog in the web interface shows the three steps.
  • Switching the option on renames all detectors at once, as a single batch.
  • A detector without a usable location gets IDs based on its serial number, e.g. sensor.genius_12345678_alarm_line. Clearing a location therefore frees the location-based IDs. The same holds for a location without any letter or digit and for detectors that still carry the placeholder Unknown location.
  • A rename is never lost while MQTT is down. The gateway remembers per detector which IDs it last announced. If a rename cannot be sent, the web interface says so, and the gateway catches up on the next MQTT connect - also after a restart.

An edit that does not change the resulting IDs (e.g. Kitchen to kitchen) does not trigger a rename. With the option off nothing changes: detectors keep their model name and Home Assistant generates the entity IDs itself.

docs.title: Areas in Home Assistant
docs.text:
The gateway suggests the detector's location as its area. Home Assistant uses the suggestion once, when it registers the device, and creates the area if it does not exist yet. Afterwards the area belongs to Home Assistant: the gateway does not move a detector to another area, and Home Assistant does not remove an area when its last device is gone.

  • After changing a location, the detector stays in its old area - with the option above it is registered again and lands in an area named after the new location. Move the device in Home Assistant if you like.
  • After deleting a detector or changing its location, the old area (e.g. Kitchen) may be left empty. Remove it in Home Assistant under Settings Areas, labels & zones.

The option needs Home Assistant 2025.10 or newer, which introduced default_entity_id in MQTT discovery.

References to the old entity IDs

Automations, scripts and dashboards that use the old entity IDs must be updated - Home Assistant does not adjust them.

The recorded history and the long-term statistics are kept: Home Assistant restores a removed entity from its entity registry and renames it, so the old data appears under the new ID. This was verified with Home Assistant 2026.10.

Two detectors with the same location ask for the same entity IDs. Home Assistant then appends _2 to the IDs of the one it registers second.

Limitations

  • Home Assistant does not confirm the rename. MQTT discovery has no acknowledgement, so the gateway knows that the new IDs were sent, not that they were applied. The progress dialog therefore ends with Sent to Home Assistant.
  • Home Assistant must be running. The gateway can only tell whether the MQTT broker is reachable, not whether Home Assistant is listening. If a rename is sent while the broker is up but Home Assistant is down, Home Assistant misses the removal, finds the entities still registered when it starts again and keeps the old IDs. The gateway does not repeat the rename in this case. Use Recreate entity IDs on the device page in Home Assistant, or change the location once more.

Applying Changes

Click Apply Settings to save. Changes take effect immediately - if MQTT is connected, updated discovery messages are published automatically. Disabling the integration removes the device from Home Assistant immediately (see warning above).

MQTT Topics Reference

See Home Assistant Auto-Discovery for topic structure and payload formats.

docs.title: Related Documentation
docs.text: Integration with Home Assistant is described in detail in Smart Home Integration.

docs.title: Simple Alarm Publishing
docs.text:
The Simple Alarm Publishing collapsible card configures a simple, platform-agnostic alarm notification via MQTT - and optionally a second topic for battery warnings and faults.

Is the gateway still there?

The topics keep their last value when the gateway goes offline. Watch the device status topic (online / offline) to notice an outage.

Administrator Access Required

Smart home integration settings can only be modified by users with administrator privileges.

Enable simple alarm publishing

Toggle to enable/disable publishing alarm events to a central topic.

Alarm Topic

MQTT topic where alarm state is published when any smoke detector triggers an alarm.

Valid MQTT Topic Syntax
  • 1-64 characters
  • no wildcards + or #
  • cannot start or end with /
  • no double slashes //
  • no special characters except /, -, and _

Global Alarm State Topic

See Global Alarm State Topic for the exact payload format.

Enable simple fault publishing

Toggle to enable/disable publishing faults reported by smoke detectors - battery low, device faults, radio link faults and dismounting - to a central topic.

Fault Topic

MQTT topic where the status summary of all smoke detectors is published whenever a smoke detector's status changes. Same syntax rules as the alarm topic.

Global Fault State Topic

See Global Fault State Topic for the exact payload format.

docs.title: MQTT Value Tree
docs.text:
The MQTT Value Tree collapsible card switches on a third way of publishing, meant for smart home systems other than Home Assistant: every value of every smoke detector and alarm line gets a topic of its own, with a plain text payload.

Enable MQTT value tree

Toggle to enable/disable the value tree. Switching it off clears the topics it published.

Root Topic

The topic under which the tree is published. Leave it empty for the default genius-gateway/<mac> (the gateway's MAC address without colons). Same syntax rules as the alarm topic. Changing it clears the topics under the old root.

Topics of the value tree

See MQTT Value Tree for the list of topics and when they are published.

docs.title: Network Time (NTP)
docs.text: Network Time Protocol (NTP) synchronizes the device's internal clock with internet time servers, ensuring accurate timestamps for logs, alarms, and event recording.

docs.title: NTP Status
docs.text: The status section displays various time synchronization information, updated every 5 seconds.

docs.title: Change NTP Settings
docs.text:
Click the Change NTP Settings collapsible section to configure NTP parameters.

Administrator Access Required

NTP settings can only be modified by users with administrator privileges.

docs.title: Enable NTP
docs.text: Toggle checkbox to enable or disable NTP time synchronization.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
NTP server hostname or IPv4 address.

  • Format: Valid domain name or IPv4 address (3-64 characters)
  • Default: pool.ntp.org (public NTP pool server)

docs.title: Pick Time Zone
docs.text:
Select your local timezone from the dropdown list. The device uses this to convert UTC time to your local time.

Daylight Saving Time

The selected timezone automatically handles daylight saving time transitions where applicable.

docs.title: Applying Changes
docs.text: Click Apply Settings to save and apply the NTP configuration. The device will apply the new timezone and NTP server settings immediately and begin time synchronization.

docs.title: Hardware Setup
docs.text: Choose either the experimental setup to test the functions of Genius Gateway, or the Genius Gateway PCB to put Genius Gateway into operation.

docs.title: IDE and Plugins
docs.text:
The project is based on the PlatformIO build system. Unfortunately, PlatformIO does not support Espressif Arduino 3.x .

Fortunately, there is pioarduino : a community-maintained fork of the PlatformIO IDE for Visual Studio Code that provides support for Espressif microcontrollers, especially the newer ESP32 boards and the latest Arduino Core for them.

  1. Download and install Microsoft VSCode .
  2. Install Pioarduino IDE (pioarduino) extension from within VSCode.
  3. Install Node.js (a current LTS version). The firmware build also builds the web interface, which requires Node.js.

docs.title: Clone GitHub Project
docs.text:
1. Clone the project to your local environment 

    git clone https://github.com/hmbacher/genius-gateway.git

  2. Open the project in VSCode 

    cd genius-gateway
code .

docs.title: Target board
docs.text:
Choose the board you are working with in platformio.ini file by (un)commenting the appropriate default_envs options: 

[platformio]
description = Genius Gateway - A gateway for Hekatron Genius Plus X smoke detectors
data_dir = data
extra_configs =
    factory_settings.ini
    features.ini
;default_envs = esp32-s3-devkitc-1
;default_envs = esp32-s3-devkitc-1-n8r2
;default_envs = seeed-xiao-esp32s3
default_envs = gg-v1_0

Environment Board gg-v1_0 Genius Gateway PCB 1.0 (Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3, 8 MB PSRAM) with its CC1101 wiring as a preset seeed-xiao-esp32s3 Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 (8 MB PSRAM) with custom wiring esp32-s3-devkitc-1-n8r2 ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 with 2 MB PSRAM esp32-s3-devkitc-1 ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 without PSRAM

PSRAM

Genius Gateway is designed around boards with PSRAM. The esp32-s3-devkitc-1 environment builds and runs without PSRAM, but is limited to 10 devices. See Memory Considerations for details.

docs.title: SPI bus wiring
docs.text:
The SPI bus and GDO signal pins of the CC1101 are not set at build time. They are configured at runtime in the web interface, see Pin Configuration.

The gg-v1_0 environment already contains the wiring of the Genius Gateway PCB as a preset, so no pin configuration is needed there. All other environments start without a pin assignment, which has to be set once after the first startup.

docs.title: More build options
docs.text:
The platformio.ini file is the main file for controlling the software build. It references two additional files whose content is evaluated by the build system:

  • features.ini
  • factory_settings.ini

Critical

Settings can be made in the listed files that affect the build and the later functionality of the Genius Gateway.

For regular functionality, no adjustments beyond those described above need to be made.

docs.title: Build Software
docs.text: Start the Build task for the corresponding project environment (target device):

docs.title: Flash Software
docs.text:
Make sure you have properly connected the board to your computer via USB cable. A serial device must appear in the systems devices.

Start the Upload and Monitor Task and pick the right serial interface if asked:

After the device has been successfully flashed, it will restart and you will see its serial output in VSCode's terminal window.

docs.title: Initial Configuration of Genius Gateway
docs.text:
After the first startup, the device has the settings stored in factory_settings.ini .

The device creates its own WiFi network with the SSID Genius-Gateway-XXX and the password genius-gateway. The Genius Gateway web interface can be accessed via the IP address 192.168.4.1 .

The default password for the admin account is admin.

docs.title: WiFi Settings
docs.text: Genius Gateway can be integrated into an existing WiFi network.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
By default, two users are created: an admin account with elevated privileges and a guest account with limited privileges.

Additional users can be created with their own username and password. See the Users page for details on managing user accounts.

docs.title: Change JWT Secret
docs.text:
For security reasons, it is strongly recommended to change the default JWT (JSON Web Token) secret after initial setup. The JWT secret is used to sign authentication tokens and should be unique for your gateway.

To change the JWT token, navigate to the Security Settings section on the Users page and enter a new JWT secret value. Note that changing the JWT secret will sign out all users immediately.

How to get a secure JWT Secret

You can generate a cryptographically strong JWT secret using an online tool such as RandomKeygen . Use a Fort Knox Password (256-bit or higher) for maximum security.

docs.title: MQTT
docs.text: For integration into a smart home system, the local MQTT broker must be configured. See the MQTT Settings page for details on configuring the MQTT connection.

docs.title: System
docs.text: The System pages provide comprehensive information about the Genius Gateway's hardware status, performance metrics, diagnostic tools, and firmware management capabilities.

docs.title: System Status
docs.text: The System Status page displays detailed information about the gateway's current operating state, hardware configuration, and resource utilization. This information updates in real-time via WebSocket connection.

docs.title: System Information
docs.text: The status page displays a lot of self-explaning system related information.

docs.title: Device Management Actions
docs.text: At the bottom of the System Status page, several management actions are available:

docs.title: Restart
docs.text: Performs a software restart of the device. The device will reboot and reconnect to the network automatically.

docs.title: Factory Reset
docs.text:
Resets all settings to factory defaults, including: - WiFi configuration - User accounts - MQTT settings - Device and alarm line configurations - All other custom settings

Permanent Action

Factory reset cannot be undone. All configuration data will be permanently erased. The device will restart with default system settings (from factory_settings.ini) and not Genius PLus X related configuration.

docs.title: Radio (CC1101)
docs.text: The CC1101 page provides runtime SPI pin configuration for the CC1101 radio transceiver. This page is only accessible to administrators.

docs.title: Top-Bar Radio Indicator
docs.text:
The radio status is reflected by a persistent icon in the navigation bar that links to this page from anywhere in the interface:

Icon Meaning Loading - radio status not yet received Radio listening (RX) - normal operating state Radio transmitting (TX) Radio initializing Radio error - check pin configuration Radio not configured

docs.title: Pin Configuration
docs.text:
The SPI bus and GDO signal pins used by the CC1101 transceiver can be changed at runtime without reflashing the firmware. Pin settings are persisted on the gateway and survive reboots.

If the board has predefined wiring presets, a Wiring dropdown lets you select one and fills in all pins automatically. Select Custom to configure each pin individually.

Pin Role CSN SPI chip select (active low) SCK SPI clock MOSI SPI data from ESP32 to CC1101 MISO SPI data from CC1101 to ESP32 GDO0 Packet signal - asserted when a packet has been received

To change pins:

  1. Select a wiring preset or choose Custom and pick a GPIO for each pin. Reserved GPIOs are highlighted in red and cannot be selected; strapping pins are highlighted in orange as a caution
  2. Click Test & Save - the gateway probes the CC1101 over the new pin assignment and saves the configuration if the self-test passes
  3. The top-bar radio indicator updates to reflect the new state

Pin conflicts rejected

Assigning the same GPIO to two different pins is blocked before any change is applied.

Existing installations unaffected (Genius Gateway hardware only)

If no pin configuration has been saved, the firmware uses the compile-time defaults from platformio.ini. Upgrading from an older firmware leaves pin assignments unchanged until you explicitly apply new ones via this page.

docs.title: System Metrics
docs.text:
The System Metrics page provides real-time graphical visualization of system performance over time.

Metrics collection begins when the web interface connects to the device and continues while it remains open, with data displayed as line charts. Charts update automatically as new data arrives via WebSocket.

Performance Monitoring

Monitor these metrics to identify resource constraints, memory leaks, or thermal issues. Sudden spikes or trends may indicate problems that need attention.

docs.title: Memory (Heap) Usage
docs.text:
Line chart showing:

  • Used: Amount of heap memory currently allocated (primary line)
  • Max Alloc: Maximum contiguous block available for allocation (secondary line)

Y-axis scale adjusts to the total heap size.

docs.title: PSRAM Usage
docs.text:
Line chart showing PSRAM utilization over time.

Info

This chart is only displayed if PSRAM is available on the device.

docs.title: File System Usage
docs.text: Line chart showing the amount of flash storage used by the file system over time.

docs.title: Core Temperature
docs.text: Line chart showing the ESP32 chip temperature in degrees Celsius over time. Useful for monitoring thermal performance and detecting overheating conditions.

docs.title: Core Dump
docs.text: The Core Dump page allows you to download diagnostic information captured when the device experiences a crash or exception. This data can be helpful for debugging firmware issues.

docs.title: Core Dump Information
docs.text:
A core dump is a snapshot of the device's memory at the moment of a crash, including:

  • Register states
  • Stack trace
  • Memory contents
  • Exception cause

docs.title: Downloading Core Dumps
docs.text:
If a core dump is available:

  1. Click the Download Core Dump (coredump.bin) button to download the core dump file to your computer
  2. This file can be analyzed using ESP-IDF tools to determine the crash cause

Info

If no core dump is available, the message "No core dump available." is displayed.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
The Migrations page shows what automatic config upgrades the gateway has performed across firmware versions. When you flash a new firmware, the gateway may need to transform older config files into the shape the new firmware expects - for example, splitting one combined file into two dedicated ones - and it does so without you having to re-enter anything in the UI.

Administrator Access Required

The Migrations page is only accessible to users with administrator privileges.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
Every migration the firmware knows about appears on the page in one of four states:

State What it means Applied The migration ran successfully and is recorded. It will never run again on this device. Failed Something went wrong while applying. The gateway will normally try again on the next reboot. Pending The migration hasn't run yet but should - it will be applied on the next reboot. Not applicable The migration doesn't apply to this device. Typically the old config file it would transform doesn't exist here (e.g. on a fresh install).

On a device upgraded from an older firmware that needed migration work, you will see Applied rows for the migrations that completed. On a fresh install of the same firmware, those same migrations show as Not applicable instead - there was nothing on disk to convert.

A small critical badge appears next to the state when a migration is essential for the gateway to start up safely.

docs.title: If something failed
docs.text:
If any migration shows as Failed, a warning banner appears at the top of the page. The gateway normally retries failed migrations automatically on the next reboot. If a migration fails several times in a row, the gateway records it as given up to avoid an infinite retry loop. The Retry on next reboot button at the top of the page clears that marker so the gateway will try again after you reboot the device.

Pressing Retry does not apply migrations immediately - it only clears the give-up marker. You still need to reboot the device. Migrations are designed so that re-running them after a partial failure is safe.

In the rare case that a critical migration fails, the gateway will refuse to boot rather than run with inconsistent configuration. You will see this in the serial log. Recovery typically requires a factory reset or a fresh firmware flash.

docs.title: Firmware Update
docs.text:
The Firmware Update page provides two methods for updating the gateway firmware: downloading releases from GitHub or manually uploading firmware files.

Administrator Access Required

Firmware update features are only accessible to users with administrator privileges.

docs.title: Top-Bar Update Indicator
docs.text:
A persistent icon in the navigation bar shows the current firmware update status. It is only displayed for administrators when the download firmware feature is enabled:

Icon Meaning Checking for updates :tabler-cloud-check: Firmware is up to date - click to re-check Update available - click to install :tabler-cloud-off:{ style="color: #ff9800" } Cannot reach GitHub - check internet connection

A toast notification appears on a successful re-check only when triggered manually (not during the automatic hourly poll).

docs.title: GitHub Firmware Manager
docs.text: The GitHub Firmware Manager lists all firmware releases published to the project's GitHub repository and lets you install any of them with one click.

docs.title: Release List
docs.text: Each release row shows the version tag and a list of available firmware assets. When the device's current version is known, the row matching the installed version is highlighted - indicating that version is already running.

docs.title: Build Target Filtering
docs.text:
The device reports its build target (e.g. seeed-xiao-esp32s3) as part of the API response. Assets whose filename contains the build target are marked as compatible; any others are incompatible.

By default only compatible assets are shown. If a release contains incompatible assets a toggle labelled Hide incompatible build targets appears above the list. It is checked by default, hiding incompatible assets; unchecking it reveals them.

No toggle shown

If all assets across all releases are compatible with the device, the toggle is not displayed at all.

docs.title: Installing a Release
docs.text:
1. Find the release you want and click the install button next to the desired .bin asset.
  2. A confirmation dialog appears listing the target URL.
    • For a compatible asset the dialog uses the standard warning style.
    • For an incompatible asset the dialog uses a red/error style and warns that the firmware was not built for this hardware variant.
  3. Click Update (or Update anyway for incompatible assets) to start the download. The device fetches the binary from GitHub, writes it to flash, and restarts automatically.

docs.title: Upload Firmware
docs.text: The Upload Firmware section allows manual installation of firmware files from your local computer.

docs.title: Firmware Validation
docs.text:
The upload service performs several validation checks to ensure firmware safety:

  • File Type Verification: Only .bin (firmware binary) and .md5 (checksum) files are accepted
  • Firmware Size Check: Minimum size of 1 MB required (for the .bin file) to be recognized as valid firmware

  • Target Hardware Validation: The firmware header is checked to ensure it matches the device's chip type (ESP32, ESP32-S2, ESP32-C3, or ESP32-S3)

    Target Compatibility

    Firmware compiled for a different ESP32 chip variant will be rejected during upload. For example, firmware built for ESP32-S3 cannot be uploaded to an ESP32-S2 device.

  • MD5 Checksum: If an .md5 file is uploaded before the firmware, the binary is verified against the checksum during upload

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text:
• .bin: Compiled firmware binary file (minimum 1 MB)
  • .md5: MD5 checksum file (32-character hex string)

The .md5 file should contain only the 32-character MD5 hash of the corresponding .bin file.

docs.title: Uploading Firmware
docs.text:
To upload firmware manually:

  1. (Optional) Upload MD5 checksum first:

    • Click Choose File and select the .md5 file
    • The checksum is stored and will be used to verify the firmware

  2. Upload the firmware binary:

    • Click Choose File and select the .bin file
    • A confirmation dialog appears: "Are you sure you want to overwrite the existing firmware with a new one?"
    • Click Upload to confirm and begin the installation

  3. Firmware Installation:

    • The device validates the firmware header
    • If an MD5 checksum was provided, the firmware is verified against it
    • The firmware is written to the device's flash memory
    • Upon successful completion, the device automatically restarts and executes the newly installed firmware

Failure Recovery

If the firmware validation or flashing fails or the device becomes unresponsive after an update:

  • After upload: If validation fails (wrong chip type, MD5 mismatch), the upload is rejected and the current firmware remains active
  • During flashing: If persisting the new firmware to flash memory fails, the current firmware remains active after restart
  • After restart: If the new firmware crashes or fails to boot properly, the device will likely enter a boot loop. Then a manual recovery is required, i.e. flashing a working firmware via USB using the build and flash instructions.

No Automatic Rollback

The firmware does not implement automatic rollback to the previous version. Always test new firmware builds on a development device before updating production devices.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
The Users page allows administrators to manage user accounts and configure security settings for the Genius Gateway. Each user can have different privilege levels, and authentication is secured using JWT (JSON Web Token) technology.

Administrator Access Required

The Users page is only accessible to users with administrator privileges. Non-admin users are automatically redirected to the home page.

docs.title: Manage Users
docs.text: The user management section displays all configured users in a table format and provides controls for adding, editing, and deleting user accounts.

docs.title: User List
docs.text:
The user table displays the following information for each user:

  • Username: The user's login name
  • Admin: Displays a key icon if the user has administrator privileges
  • Edit: Action buttons for modifying or removing the user

docs.title: Adding a User
docs.text:
To create a new user account:

  1. Click the button in the top-right corner of the user list

  2. The "Add User" dialog opens

  3. Configure the user details:

    Username

    Enter a unique username (3-32 characters) for the new account.

    Warning

    The username cannot be changed after creation.

    Password Enter a password for the user.

    Warning

    The password field can be left empty if desired, though this is not recommended for security reasons.

    Is Admin? Check this box to grant administrator privileges to the user. Administrators have full access to all gateway features and settings, including user management.

  4. Click Save to create the user

After saving, the new user appears in the user list and can immediately log in with the configured credentials.

docs.title: Editing a User
docs.text:
To modify an existing user account:

  1. Click the Edit button next to the user you want to modify

  2. The "Edit User" dialog opens with the current settings

  3. Modify the desired settings:

    Username The username field is displayed but cannot be modified for existing users.

    Password Enter a new password to change the user's credentials. Leave the field unchanged to keep the current password.

    Is Admin? Check or uncheck this box to change the user's administrator privileges.

  4. Click Save to apply the changes

Privilege Changes

Changes to administrator privileges take effect immediately. If you remove admin privileges from your own account while logged in, you will lose access to the Users page and other admin-only features until you log in with an admin account.

docs.title: Deleting a User
docs.text:
Permanent Action

Deleting a user is permanent and cannot be undone. The user will be immediately logged out if currently connected.

To remove a user account:

  1. Click the Delete button next to the user you want to remove
  2. A confirmation dialog appears
  3. Click Yes to confirm deletion, or Abort to cancel

The user account is immediately removed and can no longer be used to access the gateway.

docs.title: Security Settings
docs.text: The Security Settings section allows you to configure the JWT (JSON Web Token) secret used for authentication token signing.

docs.title: JWT Secret
docs.text:
The JWT secret is a cryptographic key used to sign and verify authentication tokens. This ensures that tokens cannot be forged or tampered with.

Default Value: A random string generated during factory setup

To change the JWT secret:

  1. Enter a new value in the JWT Secret field
  2. Click Apply Settings to save the change

Sign-Out Warning

If you modify the JWT Secret, all users will be signed out immediately. All active sessions will be invalidated, and users must log in again with their credentials.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Protect the JWT Secret: Never share or expose the JWT secret. It should be treated as a highly sensitive credential.
  • Use Strong Secrets: The JWT secret should be a long, random string to ensure maximum security.
  • Change After Setup: Consider changing the default JWT secret during initial setup to ensure unique security for your gateway.
  • Regular Updates: For enhanced security, consider changing the JWT secret periodically (this will require all users to log in again).

docs.title: Authentication Flow
docs.text:
The token-based authentication provides secure access control without requiring passwords to be sent with every request.

When a user logs in to the Genius Gateway:

  1. The user provides their username and password
  2. The gateway validates the credentials against the user database
  3. If valid, a JWT token is generated and signed with the JWT secret
  4. The token is sent to the user's browser and included in all subsequent requests
  5. The gateway verifies the token signature on each request to ensure authenticity
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User Browser
    participant Gateway as Genius Gateway

    Note over User,Gateway: Login Phase
    User->>Gateway: POST /login (username, password)
    Gateway->>Gateway: Validate credentials
    Gateway->>Gateway: Generate JWT token<br/>signed with JWT secret
    Gateway-->>User: Return JWT token
    User->>User: Store token in browser

    Note over User,Gateway: Authenticated Requests
    User->>Gateway: API Request<br/>(Authorization: Bearer <token>)
    Gateway->>Gateway: Verify token signature<br/>using JWT secret
    Gateway-->>User: Return response (if valid)

    Note over User,Gateway: Token Invalidation
    User->>Gateway: Logout or JWT secret changed
    User->>User: Clear stored token
    User-->>Gateway: Must re-authenticate

docs.title: WiFi Configuration
docs.text: The WiFi configuration allows you to connect the Genius Gateway to your local network and optionally provide an Access Point for initial setup or fallback connectivity. This page covers both WiFi Station (client) mode and Access Point mode configuration.

docs.title: WiFi Station
docs.text: The WiFi Station mode connects the Genius Gateway to your existing WiFi network as a client device. This is the primary mode for integrating the gateway into your home network.

docs.title: WiFi Connection
docs.text: When you access the WiFi Station page, you'll see the current connection status at the top of the page.

docs.title: Not Connected
docs.text: When the gateway is not connected to any WiFi network, the status shows as "Inactive":

docs.title: Connected
docs.text: When successfully connected to a WiFi network, the status shows detailed connection information:

docs.title: Settings & Networks
docs.text:
Access Requirements

WiFi settings can only be modified by users with administrator privileges.

The Settings & Networks section allows you to configure the hostname and manage known WiFi networks.

docs.title: Host Name (mDNS)
docs.text:
Format: 3-32 characters

The hostname is used for mDNS (multicast DNS) resolution, allowing you to access the gateway using a friendly name like http://hostname.local instead of an IP address.

docs.title: WiFi Connection Mode
docs.text:
The connection mode determines how the gateway selects which network to connect to when multiple networks are available:

  • Offline: WiFi connection is disabled
  • Signal Strength: Automatically connects to the network with the strongest signal

  • Priority (Sequence): Connects to networks based on the order in the list (drag-and-drop to reorder)

    Priority Mode

    When using Priority mode with multiple networks configured, arrange the networks according to their priority (most important first) using the drag-and-drop handles.

docs.title: Initial Configuration
docs.text:
When no WiFi networks are configured, you'll see a message:

No WiFi networks configured yet. Scan for available networks or add one manually.

Use the Scan or Add buttons to configure your first network.

docs.title: Adding WiFi Networks
docs.text: The gateway supports up to 5 configured WiFi networks. You can add networks in two ways:

docs.title: Scanning for Networks
docs.text:
1. Click the Scan button in the top-right corner

  2. The gateway scans for available WiFi networks

  3. After scanning completes, a list of discovered networks appears

  4. Click on a network from the list to proceed with configuration

  5. The "Add network" dialog opens with the SSID pre-filled

Network Limit

If you already have 5 networks configured, you'll see a message: "You have reached the maximum number of networks. Please delete one to add another."

docs.title: Manual Entry
docs.text:
1. Click the Add button in the top-right corner

  2. The "Add network" dialog opens

  3. Configure the network parameters:

    SSID Enter the network name (case-sensitive)

    Password Enter the WiFi password (if the network is secured)

    Password Storage

    WiFi passwords are stored unencrypted in the device's file system. Ensure physical access to the device is restricted.

    Use Static IP Enable this option to configure a static IP address instead of using DHCP

    Static IP Configuration (only when "Use Static IP" is enabled):

    • Local IP: The static IP address to assign to the gateway
    • Gateway IP: The network gateway address
    • Subnet Mask: The network subnet mask
    • DNS IP 1: Primary DNS server address
    • DNS IP 2: Secondary DNS server address (optional)

  4. Click Save to add the network

The new network appears in the list with a badge indicating either "Static" or "DHCP" configuration.

docs.title: Managing Networks
docs.text:
Each configured network in the list displays:

  • Drag handle: Reorder networks (only visible when Connection Mode is set to "Priority")
  • SSID: Network name
  • Configuration badge: Shows "Static" (static IP) or "DHCP" (automatic IP)
  • Edit button: Modify network settings
  • Delete button: Remove the network from the list

docs.title: Editing a Network
docs.text:
1. Click the Edit button next to the network you want to modify
  2. The "Edit network" dialog opens with current settings
  3. Modify the desired parameters
  4. Click Save to apply changes

docs.title: Deleting a Network
docs.text:
1. Click the Delete button next to the network you want to remove
  2. A confirmation dialog appears: "Are you sure you want to delete network '[SSID]'?"
  3. Click Delete to confirm removal

docs.title: Reordering Networks (Priority Mode)
docs.text:
When Connection Mode is set to "Priority (Sequence)":

  1. Click and hold the grip handle on the left side of a network entry
  2. Drag the network to the desired position
  3. Release to drop the network in its new position
  4. The gateway will attempt to connect to networks in the displayed order

docs.title: Applying Settings
docs.text:
After making changes to the hostname, connection mode, or network list:

  1. The Apply Settings button becomes enabled
  2. Click Apply Settings to save your configuration
  3. A notification confirms: "Wi-Fi settings updated."
  4. If WiFi connection settings changed, you may see: "Reconnecting shortly as new WiFi settings will be applied in X seconds."

Connection Changes

When changing WiFi settings, the gateway will reconnect to apply the new configuration. This may cause a brief disconnection.

docs.title: When the Connection Is Lost
docs.text:
The gateway reconnects by itself, however long the outage lasts:

  • Every 5 seconds it scans for the configured networks and connects to the one the connection mode selects
  • A connection attempt has 20 seconds to end with an IP address. Otherwise it is dropped and the gateway starts over with a new scan - also when it is connected to the access point but gets no IP address
  • After 5 minutes offline, and again every 5 minutes, the gateway restarts its WiFi interface

The gateway itself is never restarted because of a missing WiFi connection. It keeps receiving its smoke detectors while it is offline, and reports again as soon as the connection is back.

docs.title: Access Point
docs.text: The Access Point mode allows the Genius Gateway to create its own WiFi network, enabling direct connection from your devices. This is useful for initial setup when no WiFi credentials are known, or as a fallback when the primary WiFi connection is unavailable.

docs.title: Access Point Status
docs.text: The status section displays current Access Point information:

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The AP status can be:

  • Active (green): Access Point is running and accepting connections
  • Inactive (red): Access Point is disabled
  • Lingering (yellow): Access Point is in the process of shutting down

docs.title: Status Information
docs.text:
When the Access Point is active, the following information is displayed:

  • IP Address: The gateway's IP address on the AP network (typically 192.168.4.1)
  • MAC Address: The Access Point's MAC address
  • AP Clients: Number of devices currently connected to the Access Point

docs.title: Access Point Settings
docs.text:
Access Requirements

Access Point settings can only be modified by users with administrator privileges.

docs.title: Provide Access Point ...
docs.text:
This setting controls when the Access Point is available:

  • Always: Access Point is permanently enabled
  • When WiFi Disconnected: Access Point activates only when the gateway cannot connect to any configured WiFi network (fallback mode)
  • Never: Access Point is permanently disabled

Recommended Setting

"When WiFi Disconnected" is recommended for most users, as it provides automatic fallback connectivity while conserving resources when WiFi station is connected.

docs.title: SSID
docs.text:
Format: 2-32 characters

The network name (SSID) that will be broadcast by the Access Point. Choose a unique name to identify your gateway's network.

docs.title: Password
docs.text:
The WiFi password required to connect to the Access Point. Leave empty for an open (unsecured) network.

Security

For security reasons, it's strongly recommended to set a password for your Access Point.

Password Storage

WiFi passwords are stored unencrypted in the device's file system. Ensure physical access to the device is restricted.

docs.title: Preferred Channel
docs.text:
Range: 1-13

The WiFi channel number the Access Point will use. If experiencing interference, try changing to a different channel. Channels 1, 6, and 11 are commonly recommended as they don't overlap.

docs.title: Max Clients
docs.text:
Range: 1-8

The maximum number of devices that can simultaneously connect to the Access Point. Lower values reduce resource usage.

docs.title: Local IP
docs.text:
Format: Valid IPv4 address

The IP address the gateway will use on the Access Point network. Standard configuration is 192.168.4.1.

docs.title: Gateway IP
docs.text:
Format: Valid IPv4 address

The gateway IP address for the Access Point network. This is typically the same as the Local IP (192.168.4.1).

docs.title: Subnet Mask
docs.text:
Format: Valid IPv4 address

The subnet mask for the Access Point network. Standard configuration is 255.255.255.0.

docs.title: Applying Access Point Settings
docs.text:
After modifying Access Point settings:

  1. Click the Apply Settings button at the bottom of the form
  2. All fields are validated:
    • SSID must be 2-32 characters
    • Channel must be 1-13
    • Max Clients must be 1-8
    • All IP addresses must be valid IPv4 format
  3. If validation passes, a notification confirms: "Access Point settings updated."
  4. If validation fails, error messages appear below the invalid fields in red text

Configuration Tips

  • Use the default IP configuration (192.168.4.1) unless you have specific networking requirements
  • Set Max Clients to match your expected usage to optimize performance
  • Choose a channel with minimal interference from nearby networks
